Every mnemonic with its bits and description is listed on the [extension site](https://retrocorelabs.github.io/vs-extension-nd110-uc/docs/variants/nd5000/).

## How the bits of a token are written

`encoding.parts` is a list of 8 strings of 6 octal digits, **most significant 16-bit group first**. A token sets the bits that are 1 in its groups; the tokens of one instruction are ORed together.

A token with `field` and `value` puts `value` shifted left by the low bit of the field (see the field file); its `parts` already hold the result.

A token with `mem_code` is a memory operation. The header of the token file says how the 4-bit code is split over the word.
